set.title: Law enforcement policy starter set
set.description: Three policy structures written by Resgrid for police services and other law enforcement agencies: the use-of-force policy acknowledgment, the duty to intervene and report, and evidence handling. They carry headings and placeholders only: insert your agency's own policy text and the law that applies where you work.

protocols.name: Use-of-force policy acknowledgment
protocols.description: The structure of a use-of-force policy that every sworn member reads and acknowledges each year.

blocks.html: This is a structure for your agency's use-of-force policy. Replace each placeholder with your approved policy text before you publish it.
[Insert your agency's purpose statement and who the policy applies to.]
[Insert the definitions your policy and the law where you work use.]

blocks.title: Principles to set out in your policy

items.html: De-escalation: when and how members are expected to use it.
The standard for using force, as your law and policy define it.

blocks.title: Local law comes first
blocks.html: Your policy must follow the law and the oversight rules where you work. Have it reviewed by your legal adviser before you publish it.

protocols.name: Duty to intervene and report
protocols.description: Members step in to stop misconduct they witness and report it.

items.html: Intervenes, when it is safe to do so, to stop force or conduct that is clearly outside policy or the law.
Gives or gets medical aid for anyone who needs it.
Reports what they saw to a supervisor as soon as possible, in the way your policy sets out.

blocks.html: [Insert your agency's protection against retaliation for members who intervene or report.]

protocols.name: Evidence handling and chain of custody
protocols.description: Collecting, labelling, storing and transferring evidence so its history can always be shown.

items.html: Photograph or record each item where it was found before it is moved.
Package and seal each item separately, and label it with the case number, the item number, who collected it, when and where.
Start the chain-of-custody record at the moment of collection.
Record who handed the item over, who received it, when, and why.
Check that the seal is intact; report a broken seal at once.

blocks.html: [Insert your agency's storage, retention and disposal rules.]
